claims.statement: The provisional Welsh Government first-year comparison reconstructs to 2,402 and 1,725 casualties, an exact change of -33850/1201 percent, compatible with the published 28% lower.
Later frozen official routes give -31350/1201 percent (StatsWales) and -11580/479 percent (DfT collision rows) for the same nominal comparison.

Three hypothetical worlds reproduce the observed aggregates (2402, 1725) yet imply affected-road effects of -50%, 0% and +100%; within the frozen corpus and admitted model class the effect and its sign are not identified.
No empirical identified interval or sign restriction is registered; the witness values are not bounds.

claimCeiling: The positive 28 percent attribution remains a challenged, unsupported policy claim. The case supplies a candidate, corpus-specific counterexample; it does not establish the policy's true effect, a new general theorem, exhaustive novelty, independent reproduction or peer review.
notClaimed: that the policy failed, succeeded or had no effect
that -50%, 0% or +100% are estimates or bounds
that every future design is non-identified
